notes: The remaining check, 'nano1 needs at least 4.5 V but 3V3 is on 3.3 V', is not a real problem for this manual, so I kept the 3V3 wires. The 4.5 V minimum is the board's supply range on VIN/VUSB. The checker is reading the 3V3 pin as a power input. Here both Nano 33 IoT boards are powered at 5 V from the computer over USB. The 3V3 pin is the board's 3.3 V output, and the tutorial's image uses it as the I2C pull-up source. Moving the pull-ups to VUSB (5 V) would put 5 V on 3.3 V-only I2C pins, which is worse. So I kept 3V3 as the image shows.

bb2 carries the SDA line and its pull-up, so it is no longer unconnected. The tutorial lists two mini breadboards but the image shows none. I put the SCL line and r1 on bb1 and the SDA line and r2 on bb2, each with its own 3V3 rail. This needs a 7th jumper wire (wire7, a second red 3V3 wire), within the 10 in the parts list.
The SDA/SCL pins are as in the image: A4 is SDA (yellow) and A5 is SCL (teal) on both boards. GND is joined between the boards with the brown wire.
The USB cable has no ports in the catalogue, so the USB edges use a null port on the cable side and the board's USB port.
